title: Add onboard slice runbook, deterministic profile anchors, and automated release subscriptions
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an automated onboarding runbook for sampled intake slices, deterministic profile anchors for stable versioning, and a release subscription webhook that compacts and signs changelogs for downstream consumers. Includes migration for existing profiles and examples for the CLI and Console.
body:
Context and motivation:

We see two recurring pain points in model intake: 1) onboarding profiles vary wildly between runs which makes changelogs noisy and rollouts unpredictable, and 2) Product/Docs teams need a concise, signed changelog feed (compact, stable IDs) that they can subscribe to for release announcements and compliance audits. This PR introduces three cooperating pieces to address those problems: (A) an onboard-slice runbook generator that samples representative traffic slices and produces a lightweight runbook with test prompts, profile snapshots and perf baselines; (B) deterministic profile anchors — a compact, canonical fingerprint and affinity anchor for each sampled profile to make diffs stable across re-ingests; and (C) a release subscription webhook that compacts changelogs into short digests, attaches a signed release stamp, and publishes to a configurable subscriber list (email/Slack/webhook).

What this changes (high-level):
- New CLI command: `redwood model onboard-runbook --slice <cohort>` which produces runbook/manifest and uploads to registry.
- Profile anchor computation: stable fingerprint algorithm (sha256 over canonicalized metadata + a trimmed perf vector) plus a short humanizable anchor id (e.g. p-7f3e).
- Changelog compactor and signer: takes the delta between profile anchors and emits a compact summary with tokenized highlights, footprint estimates, and an immutability stamp. The compactor also strips noisy ephemeral fields.
- Release subscriber: configurable per-repo/topic, supports signed webhooks and manual preview flows.
- Migration shim to re-anchor recent profiles and populate anchor->manifest index.

Checklist:
- [x] CLI: onboard-runbook command, help text, integration tests
- [x] Server: anchor computation + index (lightweight, append-only)
- [x] Automation: changelog compactor + signer + subscription publisher
- [x] Docs: console how-to and quickstart snippets
- [x] Backfill: migration script to compute anchors for last 30 days
- [x] E2E tests: sample-run -> anchor -> compactor -> subscription deliver

Detailed notes and decisions:
- Anchor design: we intentionally keep the fingerprint deterministic but not globally collision-free — it's designed to be stable across identical metadata/perf, and to change only on meaningful deltas. The short anchor id is derived from the first 12 bits to keep human-friendly references. This keeps changelogs readable while enabling programmatic diffs.
- Changelog compaction heuristics: we keep top-3 perf regressions/improvements, tokenize notable capability changes (embedding dims, sequence length support), and estimate token-cost delta using the footprint estimator. Ephemeral fields like `ingest_id` and raw raw telemetry blobs are removed.
- Signing: HMAC using registry signing keys (integration already exists; this PR plugs into the key manager). Webhook subscribers can validate using published public key.
- Backwards compatibility: existing manifests are still readable. The migration populates the new anchor field; clients that don't care about anchors ignore it.

Commits summary:
- add: cli/onboard_runbook.py (main command and unit tests)
- add: server/anchor_index (anchor computation, lightweight index API, integration tests)
- add: compactor/compact_changelog.py (compaction + signer + unit tests)
- add: publisher/release_subscriber (subscription service + webhook delivery)
- add: migrations/20250212_anchor_backfill.py (backfill script + README)
- docs: console and cli doc edits, runbook example

Changed files (high-level):
- cli/onboard_runbook.py
- server/anchors.py
- server/api/anchors_routes.py
- compactor/compact_changelog.py
- publisher/release_subscriber.py
- migrations/20250212_anchor_backfill.py
- tests/integration/test_onboard_runbook_e2e.py
- docs/model-onboarding/runbooks.md
- examples/onboard-sample/manifest.json

Testing and CI:
- Initial CI run: unit tests passed, integration tests failed on flaky network mock (test: `test_webhook_retry_on_502`).
- Fix applied: increased mock retry window and added jitter; re-ran CI. Final CI: all checks passed (build, unit, integration, lint).

Review conversation (thread highlights):
- Arjun: "Can we ensure the anchor fingerprint ignores fields that are only set by the CLI (e.g. local path, temporary flags)? Also please add a short explainer in docs for why anchors won't change on minor perf noise."
- Maya (author): "Good catch — anchor canonicalization now strips CLI-only fields (see anchors.canonicalize()). Added docs paragraph and test to confirm invariance."
- Lena: "Migration looks heavy for large installs. Do we need a streaming backfill?"
- Maya: "Provided a streaming-mode option in the backfill script and a --batch-size flag; default is small to be safe. Also added a dry-run mode."
- Noah: "Changelog compaction seems opinionated; can we make the top-n heuristic configurable per-namespace?"
- Maya: "Made top_n configurable via registry config and exposed via CLI flag for publish. Default 3 to keep briefs concise."

Post-review changes before merge:
- Added canonicalization test fixtures for various historic manifests.
- Switched signer to use HMAC key rotation helper and added validation endpoint for subscribers.
- Fixed minor linting issues and expanded integration timeout on CI (was occasionally flaky on busy runner).

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Deploy server changes to staging and run `migrations/20250212_anchor_backfill.py --since 30d --dry-run` to validate impact.
2) Toggle subscriber feature gate on in staging and exercise sample subscription flows.
3) Run backfill streaming-mode in controlled batches in production during low-traffic window (ops runbook included in migration script README).
4) Flip feature gate and enable automatic subscription deliveries.

Risks and mitigations:
- Backfill IO pressure: mitigated via streaming backfill with configurable batch size and rate limit.
- Behavioral drift on compaction: compactor has a preview mode that emits both raw and compacted changelog for human review.
- Subscriber failures: publisher implements exponential backoff, delivery receipts, and dead-letter queue.

Related work and references:
- ENG-3482: onboarding stability playbook
- ENG-3549: compact release feed for docs and compliance

Merge outcome:
- PR was squashed and merged into main on 2025-02-18 after CI green and approvals from Arjun and Lena.

If you'd like, I can extract a short runbook for on-call ops to run the backfill (includes commands and safe defaults).
